reviews.text: I remain astounded by the speed these people work at. Insane jumps from the demo in so little time. And like the titular submarine itself it's clearly being held togehter by spit, tape and cardboard, but i'l be damned if there isn't treasure to be found here too. I have nothing but enthusiasm to see what they will continue digging up with this game. In short it scratches the itch of guns of icarus but combining it with the more slapstick coop games that is currently having a moment and wraps it in a lush and stylised visual package.

Revised review, Developer responded and refund pending. This game is not for me, but the developer was very responsive. This game is not designed for solo play, but might someday be. Biggest issue to resolve is character collision with ledges/frames - you get snagged on everything. Recommend the capsule component collisions need to be reduced, and character movement could be represented by a smaller sprite to allow better movement between upper/lower deck and through hatches, moving past stairs, etc. Basically, make the character collision smaller than the visual character. Make the collision mesh tolerate more overlap. Overall, could be fun with at least 2 players, probably better with more. Recommended roles: Pilot - pilot the submarine, avoiding obstacles and approaching loot Gunner - shoot harpoons at enemies and to recover loot Engineer - fuel and crank the engine, patch the hull when breeched, pump the bilge Quartermaster - unload harpooned loot, reinforce hull repairs, help crank engine and pump bilge as needed. As a solo player, you would have to do all of these jobs. It just doesn't work solo. Thanks for the quick response, Khaos Systems!

Played What Sub for about 3 hours with a friend and had a surprisingly good time. The atmosphere is great, the concept feels fresh, and you can tell the developers have a strong idea here. That said, the game still needs some polishing. There are bugs, some mechanics feel unfinished, and content is a bit limited right now. But even in its current state, the core gameplay loop is entertaining enough to keep you playing “just one more round.” If the developers continue updating and improving the game, this could become something really special. Definitely worth keeping an eye on.

When fishing (and combat with those pesky crabs) gets implemented, we will truly be gaming. Future looks bright.
